habitats: Unflooded upper lava tubes receiving organic debris
Sunken-cave splash debris above prolonged immersion
summary: A nonphotosynthetic decomposer fruits as pale cushions on damp, oxygenated organic deposits. Dark-tube colonies require imported carbon and never occupy permanently anaerobic cave pools. Fruit-like scent attracts occasional rondo investigation and small bites that move spores; the cushions are not its staple food. Suitable tissue feeds ecolumbre and babosa and emits no light (F9, F16, F23, F24).

chains.trait: Digestive filaments in aerated organic deposits
links: Litter, carcass fragments and transported debris provide chemical energy.
Filaments digest material externally and absorb breakdown products.
Moisture and oxygen support growth without daylight.
Carbon-starved rock and permanently anaerobic pools exclude colonies.
chains.play: Trace a dark-cave patch to its imported organic substrate without treating its presence as proof of safe air.
chains.weakness: Colonies fail when carbon or moisture runs out, under prolonged seawater immersion or in permanently anaerobic H₂S pools.
observe: Pale threads penetrate softened organic debris.
Growth ends at clean bare rock.
Cushions stop above a stagnant pool rather than covering its submerged floor.

plausibility.summary: Dark growth consumes imported organic carbon and requires a suitable oxygenated substrate. Explicitly exclude permanently anaerobic pools and prolonged immersion; an unflooded tube can still contain humid substrate.

analogues.mechanism: Extracellular digestion and absorption support growth on organic substrates without photosynthesis.

chains.trait: Fruit-scented cushions recruiting occasional spore carriers
links: Mature accessible cushions release fruit-like volatiles.
Still sheltered air retains a local scent patch.
Rondo investigates, noses or takes a small bite, picking up spores.
Subsequent movement transfers spores to other suitable deposits.
chains.play: Watch brief rondo visits near entrances and distinguish scented cushions from actual fruit.
chains.weakness: Wind disperses scent, and inaccessible deep colonies cannot depend on rondo transport.
observe: A pale cushion smells fruity without containing seeds.
Rondo noses it and leaves only a small bite.
Spore dust clings to its damp muzzle.

plausibility.summary: Rondo is an occasional sampler and spore carrier, not a staple fungivore. Fruit mimicry is a fictional specialization; deep colonies cannot assume visits from an inaccessible surface animal.

analogues.mechanism: Fungal volatiles mediate animal attraction; precise fruit mimicry and external muzzle transport are proposed extensions.

food_for: Herbivores taking occasional small investigative bites
Marine particle feeders receiving washed-out decomposition material
gameplay.gift_item: Fresh humus cushion from clean aerated litter

poison.signal: Pale tissue lacks an alkaloid warning; substrate contamination and decay remain separate concerns.

gameplay.notes: Fresh fungal tissue is distinct from its decomposing substrate. Rondo takes occasional small bites rather than relying on cushions as a staple. No colonies occur in permanently anaerobic cave pools; pale bodies reflect light and never glow.

relations.note: Grazes suitable tissue in aerated organic-fed cave patches.
Consumes soft cushions and decomposing litter.
Brief visits, nosing and occasional small bites pick up spores; this is not a staple food relationship.
May receive decomposition particles washed from tidal-fringe organic deposits.
Intercepts suspended organic breakdown material carried into coastal water.
Decomposes shed fronds in suitable humid deposits.
Shares some aerated entrance deposits while remaining nonluminous.

generator.trunk: No trunk; fleshy cushions emerge from substrate filaments.

branching.buttress: None; branching describes filaments, not woody limbs.

leaf.arrangement: Loose cushion groups over organic material

overlay_rules: Mature spore-bearing areas develop tan dust.
Waterlogged or spent cushions darken and collapse.
No bioluminescence or moon-phase colour change.

placement.slope: Protected litter floors, debris-catching benches and ledges above stagnant pools.
placement.wetness: Humid oxygenated substrate without prolonged immersion; exclude permanently anaerobic cave pools and H₂S-bearing stagnant pool substrates.
placement.soil: Aerated dead leaves, wood, carcass material or imported organic sediment.
placement.fog: Supports entrance humidity; deep growth follows local moisture, oxygen and carbon delivery.
placement.density: Patchy colonies bounded by suitable organic deposits; absent from clean rock and permanently anaerobic pools.

generator.seasonal: Fruits after moisture pulses and fresh organic delivery; deep colonies follow substrate inputs rather than sunlight.
generator.wind_response: Low cushions move little; exposed edges dry and loose spores disperse in air.

journal.en: Pale bread grows on what the cave receives. It smells of fruit, but makes no light.
journal.es: Pan pálido crece sobre lo que recibe la cueva. Huele a fruta, pero no da luz.

Compare a visited entrance cushion with an inaccessible deep colony.

secrets: A fresh deep colony points toward an organic delivery route.
Splash-zone cushions reveal debris accumulation above prolonged tidal flooding.
